content.title: Philadelphia Flyers outplay Pittsburgh Penguins in Game 1 win: Highlights
content.text: April 18, 2026Updated April 19, 2026, 1:12 a.m. ETThe Pittsburgh Penguins are back in the NHL postseason after a three-year absence, but they are loaded with playoff veterans Sidney Crosby, Evgeni Malkin, Erik Karlsson and Kris Letang.The Philadelphia Flyers ended a five-year drought and their playoff experience can't match Pittsburgh's.But in Game 1, at least, the Flyers were the better team, out-chancing the Penguins and beating them 3-2. Game 2 will be Monday in Pittsburgh.The Flyers got goals from defensemen Jamie Drysdale and Travis Sanheim and recent Michigan State forward Porter Martone. The Sanheim and Martone goals involved slick moves.Malkin had a goal and an assist for the Penguins while Crosby had no points and took four penalty minutes..USA TODAY provided live coverage of Game 1 of the Pittsburgh Penguins vs. Philadelphia Flyers first-round series. Here are highlights: Flyers vs. Penguins highlights Final score: Flyers 3, Penguins 2Flyers goalie Dan Vladar stops Anthony Mantha in the final seconds and the Flyers win 3-2. Penguins score: Bryan Rust cuts Flyers leadRust scores with 1:01 left. Flyers 3, Penguins 2 Sidney Crosby, Travis Sanheim penalizedSanheim cross-checks Crosby, who slashes Sanheim. It's Crosby's second penalty of the game. A little more than a minute left. Penguins pull Stuart SkinnerPenguins have extra attacker. Flyers score: Porter Martone adds to Flyers leadThe rookie circles back and rips a shot from the right faceoff past Stuart Skinner with 2:37 left. Flyers 3, Penguins 1 Less than five minutes left2-1 Flyers. Flyers score: Travis Sanheim gives Flyers leadSanheim gets the puck at the blue line, skates between two defenders and beats Stuart Skinner from the slot for the lead with 10 minutes left in the period. Flyers 2, Penguins 1 Flyers go on power playAnthony Mantha is called for high sticking Porter Martone. The Flyers power play ranked 32nd in the regular season. Penguins kill the penalty as Flyers get no shots. Third period underwayGame 1 is tied 1-1. Flyers have 48 seconds left on a power play. And the Penguins kill the rest. End of second period: Penguins 1, Flyers 1The Flyers control the period early and capitalize when Trevor Zegras feeds Jamie Drysdale for a goal. Evgeni Malkin later jump on a rebound and ties the game. Philadelphia leads in shots, 16-10. They will be on the power play at the start of the third period. Flyers go on power playAnthony Mantha goes off for cross-checking. Penguins score: Evgeni Malkin ties gameMalkin beats Dan Vladar on a shot that goes through Noah Cates' legs at 15:51 of the second. Penguins 1, Flyers 1 Penguins go on power playTravis Sanheim is called for interference after knocking down Sidney Crosby. A scrum breaks out. The Penguins' power play is disjointed with a Sean Couturier steal and several Penguins offsides. Flyers score: Jamie Drysdale gives Flyers leadJamie Drysdale beats Stuart Skinner through a screen to score in his playoff debut. Flyers 1, Penguins 0 Flyers forcing turnoversThe Flyers have been forcing turnovers at the Penguins' offensive blue line to get chances.Stuart Skinner strongHe stops Trevor Zegras after he steals the puck and later stops Noah Cates on a 2-on-1 break when Cates opts to shoot. Second period underwayScoreless game. Also a physical one. The Flyers outhit the Penguins 20-10. End of first period: Penguins 0, Flyers 0The Flyers appeared to score a goal, but it was waved off because Christian Dvorak fell onto Penguins goalie Stuart Skinner. Skinner looked strong in that period as the Flyers outshot the Penguins 9-5. Sidney Crosby pulls off opponent's helmetSidney Crosby is called for roughing for pulling off Jamie Drysdale's helmet, but Drysdale is called for interference. We're 4-on-4. And now we're back at full strength. Flyers goal waved offChristian Dvorak made contact with Stuart Skinner, who's down briefly but is back up. Penguins kill off penalty. Flyers go on power playKris Letang is called for tripping. The Flyers had the worst power play in the regular season. Penguins go on power playFlyers veteran Rasmus Ristolainen, making his playoff debut, is off for roughing. Philadelphia kills it off. Game underwayThis is the teams' first playoff meeting since 2018. Goalie matchupPittsburgh's Stuart Skinner vs. Philadelphia's Dan Vladar. Penguins-Flyers televisionRight now, it's on ESPNews but will switch to the main channel once the Stars-Wild game is over. Wild win the game 6-1.When is Penguins vs. Flyers Game 1?Game 1 of the Pittsburgh Penguins vs. Philadelphia Flyers first round series will be played at 8 p.m. ET on Saturday, April 18 at PPG Paints Arena in Pittsburgh.Watch NHL playoff hockey on FuboPenguins vs. Flyers: How to watch, streamDate: Saturday, April 18Time: 8 p.m. ETTV: ESPNStreaming: ESPN+, Fubo Penguins vs. Flyers start timeThe Dallas Stars-Minnesota Wild game is still going on, so the Penguins-Flyers game start is delayed. Both are being shown on ESPN. Penguins lineup Penguins vs. Flyers season seriesEach team had two wins in the season series. The Flyers' wins were in shootouts. Stuart Skinner starting in Penguins netCoach Dan Muse announced that Stuart Skinner would start Game 1 against the Flyers. He was acquired in the Tristan Jarry trade and had taken the Oilers to back-to-back Stanley Cup Finals. Arturs Silovs will back up. Hurricanes beat Senators in Game 1Frederik Andersen got the start and made 22 saves in a 2-0 victory. Logan Stankoven and Taylor Hall each had a goal and an assist.Senators captain Brady Tkachuk and Hurricanes counterpart Jordan Staal dropped the gloves off the opening faceoff.
